     9	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.QuotScheme
    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# Affine tensor-section substrate (`TensorSectionFormula`)
    13	
    14	This file collects the substrate for the affine tensor-section
    15	formula that feeds the quasi-coherent case of
    16	`Scheme.Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso` ([Stacks 01CD]; the section formula is
    17	[Stacks 01CD]/[Stacks 01CA] read on a basis of affine opens).
    18	
    19	For `A B : X.Modules` the substrate tensor `Scheme.Modules.tensorObj A B`
    20	(`Picard/TensorObjSubstrate.lean`) is the sheafification of the presheaf-of-modules
    21	tensor `P := PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj A.val B.val` of the underlying
    22	presheaves.  Objectwise, `P(V) = Γ(A, V) ⊗_{Γ(X, V)} Γ(B, V)`
    23	(`tensorPresheaf_obj`), so the sheafification unit provides a canonical
    24	`Γ(X, V)`-linear **section comparison**
    25	
    26	  `tensorSectionHom A B V : Γ(A, V) ⊗_{Γ(X, V)} Γ(B, V) ⟶ Γ(tensorObj A B, V)`
    27	
    28	for every open `V` (`tensorSectionHom`), natural in restriction
    29	(`tensorSectionHom_naturality_apply`).  Over the total space it is exactly the
    30	section multiplication `sectionsMul` of the graded-ring machinery
    31	(`tensorSectionHom_top_eq_sectionsMul`), and the substrate `tensorObj` and the
    32	section-graded `sheafTensorObj` are the same object
    33	(`tensorObjIsoSheafTensorObj`, definitional).
    34	
    35	## Contents
    36	
    37	* `tensorPresheaf` — the presheaf-of-modules tensor of the underlying presheaves.
    38	* `tensorSectionHom` — the section comparison map at an open `V`.
    39	* `tensorPresheaf_obj` — the objectwise identification of the domain as
    40	  `Γ(A, V) ⊗ Γ(B, V)`.
    41	* `tensorSectionHom_naturality_apply` — restriction naturality.
    42	* `tensorSectionHom_top_eq_sectionsMul` — the `⊤`-value is `sectionsMul`.
    43	* `tensorObjIsoSheafTensorObj` — the (definitional) `tensorObj ≅ sheafTensorObj`
    44	  bridge.
    45	* `isIso_sheafification_tensorSectionUnit` — the categorical crux: sheafifying the
    46	  presheaf comparison unit is an isomorphism (the reflective localization inverts
    47	  the unit), which is why the affine formula reduces to the presheaf-tensor
    48	  localization on a basis of affine opens.
    49	* `localizedTensorProductEquiv` / `localizedTensorProductBaseChangeEquiv` — the
    50	  algebraic localization heart, first over `R` and then over `Localization S`.
    51	* `localizedTensorProductBaseChangeEquiv_mkLinearMap_tmul` — the named pure-tensor
    52	  formula for the exact base-change equivalence.
    53	* `localizedTensorProductMap` / `isLocalizedModule_localizedTensorProductMap` — the
    54	  same result for arbitrary localization maps into an arbitrary localization algebra.
    55	
    56	## Remaining obligations (the quasi-coherent case of `pullbackTensorMap_isIso`)
    57	
    58	The genuinely hard step — promoting `tensorSectionHom A B V` to a `LinearEquiv`
    59	for quasi-coherent `A B` and *affine* `V` — is not carried out here: it requires
    60	computing the sheafification value on the basis of basic opens as a localization
    61	of the presheaf tensor, against the (currently `private`) tilde-comparison engine
    62	of `Picard/QuotScheme.lean`.  Concretely, it remains to:
    63	
    64	1. On a basic open `D(f) ⊆ V` (affine `V = Spec Γ(X, V)`), identify
    65	   `Γ(A, D(f)) = Γ(A, V)_f` and `Γ(B, D(f)) = Γ(B, V)_f` via
    66	   `isLocalizedModule_basicOpen_of_isQuasicoherent` (QuotScheme.lean), so
    67	   `P(D(f)) = Γ(A, V)_f ⊗_{Γ(X, V)_f} Γ(B, V)_f`.
    68	2. Feed `isLocalizedModule_localizedTensorProductMap` below to the two section
    69	   restriction maps.  Its codomain is already the tensor product over `Γ(X, D(f))`,
    70	   so this identifies it with `(Γ(A, V) ⊗_{Γ(X, V)} Γ(B, V))_f`, i.e. `P` is a
    71	   localizing presheaf on the basic-open basis; hence `tensorObj A B|_V` is the tilde of
    72	   `Γ(A, V) ⊗ Γ(B, V)` and `tensorSectionHom A B V` is a `LinearEquiv`.
    73	3. Transport through `Modules.pullback_app_isoTensor` (QuotScheme.lean, the
    74	   pullback side) and globalize by `isIso_of_isIso_restrict` over the affine cover,
    75	   discharging the `pullbackTensorMap_restrict` restriction coherence.
    76	
    77	### On the generality of `pullbackTensorMap_isIso`
    78	
    79	`Modules.pullbackTensorMap_isIso` is stated for *arbitrary* `A B` (no
    80	quasi-coherence hypothesis), matching the general [Stacks 01CD] statement for
    81	ringed spaces, whereas the chart chase above only closes the *quasi-coherent*
    82	case.  Its sole consumer (`pullback_moduleTensorPow_iso`) already carries
    83	`[F.IsQuasicoherent] [L.IsQuasicoherent]`, so a quasi-coherent variant assuming
    84	`[A.IsQuasicoherent] [B.IsQuasicoherent]` would be enough for that consumer and
    85	would avoid the general ringed-space stalk machinery.
    86	-/

    95	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

    97	/-- The presheaf-of-modules tensor of the underlying presheaves of `A B : X.Modules`;
    98	objectwise `Γ(A, V) ⊗_{Γ(X, V)} Γ(B, V)`.  Its sheafification is
    99	`Scheme.Modules.tensorObj A B`. -/
   100	noncomputable abbrev tensorPresheaf (A B : X.Modules) : X.PresheafOfModules :=
   101	  PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj (R := X.presheaf) A.val B.val
   102	
   103	/-- The **section comparison** at an open `V`: the `Γ(X, V)`-linear map
   104	`Γ(A, V) ⊗_{Γ(X, V)} Γ(B, V) ⟶ Γ(tensorObj A B, V)`, defined as the `V`-component of
   105	the sheafification-adjunction unit at the presheaf tensor.  On the total space it is
   106	the section multiplication `sectionsMul`; for quasi-coherent `A B` and affine `V` it
   107	is an isomorphism (the affine tensor-section formula — see the module docstring). -/
   108	noncomputable def tensorSectionHom (A B : X.Modules) (V : X.Opens) :
   109	    (tensorPresheaf A B).obj (op V) ⟶ (tensorObj A B).val.obj (op V) :=
   110	  ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).unit.app
   111	      (tensorPresheaf A B)).app (op V)
   112	
   113	/-- The domain of `tensorSectionHom` over `V` is the `Γ(X, V)`-module tensor product
   114	`Γ(A, V) ⊗ Γ(B, V)` (the objectwise formula for the presheaf-of-modules tensor). -/
   115	lemma tensorPresheaf_obj (A B : X.Modules) (V : X.Opens) :
   116	    (tensorPresheaf A B).obj (op V) =
   117	      MonoidalCategory.tensorObj (C := ModuleCat (X.presheaf.obj (op V)))
   118	        (A.val.obj (op V)) (B.val.obj (op V)) := rfl
   119	
   120	/-- Restriction naturality of the section comparison (element-wise): the comparison
   121	commutes with restriction of sections along an inclusion `V ⊆ W`. -/
   122	lemma tensorSectionHom_naturality_apply (A B : X.Modules) {V W : X.Opens} (i : op W ⟶ op V)
   123	    (x : (tensorPresheaf A B).obj (op W)) :
   124	    tensorSectionHom A B V ((tensorPresheaf A B).map i x) =
   125	      (tensorObj A B).val.map i (tensorSectionHom A B W x) :=
   126	  PresheafOfModules.naturality_apply _ i x
   127	
   128	/-- Over the total space `⊤`, the section comparison is the section multiplication
   129	`sectionsMul` of the graded-ring machinery (definitional). -/
   130	lemma tensorSectionHom_top_eq_sectionsMul (A B : X.Modules) :
   131	    tensorSectionHom A B ⊤ = sectionsMul A B := rfl
   132	
   133	/-- **Bridge (bonus).**  The substrate tensor `Scheme.Modules.tensorObj` (the object
   134	in which `pullbackTensorMap_isIso` is stated) and the section-graded
   135	`Scheme.Modules.sheafTensorObj` are the *same* object: both sheafify the
   136	presheaf-of-modules tensor of the underlying presheaves. -/
   137	noncomputable def tensorObjIsoSheafTensorObj (A B : X.Modules) :
   138	    tensorObj A B ≅ sheafTensorObj A B := Iso.refl _
   139	
   140	/-- **Categorical crux.**  Sheafifying the underlying presheaf comparison unit is an
   141	isomorphism: the reflective sheafification inverts the localization unit of
   142	`tensorPresheaf A B`.  This is the reason the affine section formula reduces to the
   143	presheaf-tensor localization on a basis of affine opens. -/
   144	lemma isIso_sheafification_tensorSectionUnit (A B : X.Modules) :
   145	    IsIso (sheafification.map
   146	      ((PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction
   147	        (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).unit.app (tensorPresheaf A B))) :=
   148	  isIso_sheafification_map_unit _

   150	/-! ## The module-localization heart -/
   151	
   152	/-- **Localization commutes with tensor product, in the form needed on basic opens.**
   153	The tensor product of the two canonical localization maps
   154	`M → S⁻¹M` and `N → S⁻¹N` is itself a localization map. Therefore its
   155	codomain is canonically equivalent to `S⁻¹(M ⊗_R N)`.
   156	
   157	The codomain here is the tensor product over `R`. For the affine section formula,
   158	compose with `IsLocalization.moduleTensorEquiv` to replace it by the tensor product
   159	over `Localization S`. This separates the localized-module universal property from
   160	the scalar-change bookkeeping. -/
   161	noncomputable def localizedTensorProductEquiv
   162	    {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] (S : Submonoid R)
   163	    (M : Type v) (N : Type w) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
   164	    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] :
   165	    LocalizedModule S (TensorProduct R M N) ≃ₗ[R]
   166	      TensorProduct R (LocalizedModule S M) (LocalizedModule S N) :=
   167	  IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv S
   168	    (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S (TensorProduct R M N))
   169	    (TensorProduct.map (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M)
   170	      (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S N))
   171	
   172	/-- On numerator pure tensors, `localizedTensorProductEquiv` is the tensor product
   173	of the two canonical localization maps. This is the formula used to identify the
   174	basic-open restriction map of the tensor presheaf. -/
   175	@[simp]
   176	lemma localizedTensorProductEquiv_mkLinearMap_tmul
   177	    {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] (S : Submonoid R)
   178	    (M : Type v) (N : Type w) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
   179	    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] (m : M) (n : N) :
   180	    localizedTensorProductEquiv S M N
   181	        (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S (TensorProduct R M N) (m ⊗ₜ[R] n)) =
   182	      LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M m ⊗ₜ[R] LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S N n := by
   183	  apply IsLocalizedModule.linearEquiv_apply
   184	
   185	/-- **The exact base-change form of tensor localization.** As an `R`-linear
   186	equivalence, localizing `M ⊗_R N` is the tensor product of `S⁻¹M` and `S⁻¹N`
   187	over `S⁻¹R = Localization S`. This is the algebraic formula consumed by the
   188	basic-open section chase. -/
   189	noncomputable def localizedTensorProductBaseChangeEquiv
   190	    {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] (S : Submonoid R)
   191	    (M : Type v) (N : Type w) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
   192	    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] :
   193	    LocalizedModule S (TensorProduct R M N) ≃ₗ[R]
   194	      TensorProduct (Localization S) (LocalizedModule S M) (LocalizedModule S N) :=
   195	  localizedTensorProductEquiv S M N ≪≫ₗ
   196	    (IsLocalization.moduleTensorEquiv S (Localization S)
   197	      (LocalizedModule S M) (LocalizedModule S N)).symm.restrictScalars R
   198	
   199	/-- The exact base-change equivalence sends a numerator pure tensor to the tensor of
   200	the two numerator classes.  Keeping this formula named avoids making affine section
   201	proofs unfold `TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul`. -/
   202	@[simp]
   203	lemma localizedTensorProductBaseChangeEquiv_mkLinearMap_tmul
   204	    {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] (S : Submonoid R)
   205	    (M : Type v) (N : Type w) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M]
   206	    [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] (m : M) (n : N) :
   207	    localizedTensorProductBaseChangeEquiv S M N
   208	        (LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S (TensorProduct R M N) (m ⊗ₜ[R] n)) =
   209	      LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S M m ⊗ₜ[Localization S]
   210	        LocalizedModule.mkLinearMap S N n := by
   211	  rw [localizedTensorProductBaseChangeEquiv, LinearEquiv.trans_apply,
   212	    localizedTensorProductEquiv_mkLinearMap_tmul]
   213	  rfl
   214	
   215	/-- The tensor product of two localization maps, with the codomain tensor product
   216	taken over an arbitrary localization algebra `A`.  This is the exact algebraic map
   217	underlying restriction from an affine open to a basic open: unlike
   218	`localizedTensorProductBaseChangeEquiv`, it does not require replacing the target
   219	modules by the canonical `LocalizedModule` model. -/
   220	noncomputable def localizedTensorProductMap
   221	    {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] (S : Submonoid R)
   222	    (A : Type uA) [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A] [IsLocalization S A]
   223	    {M : Type v} {M' : Type vM} {N : Type w} {N' : Type vN}
   224	    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N]
   225	    [AddCommMonoid M'] [Module R M'] [Module A M'] [IsScalarTower R A M']
   226	    [AddCommMonoid N'] [Module R N'] [Module A N'] [IsScalarTower R A N']
   227	    (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (g : N →ₗ[R] N') :

   229	  ((IsLocalization.moduleTensorEquiv S A M' N').symm.restrictScalars R :
   230	      TensorProduct R M' N' ≃ₗ[R] TensorProduct A M' N').toLinearMap.comp

   235	@[simp]
   236	lemma localizedTensorProductMap_tmul
   237	    {R : Type u} [CommSemiring R] (S : Submonoid R)
   238	    (A : Type uA) [CommSemiring A] [Algebra R A] [IsLocalization S A]
   239	    {M : Type v} {M' : Type vM} {N : Type w} {N' : Type vN}
   240	    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N]
   241	    [AddCommMonoid M'] [Module R M'] [Module A M'] [IsScalarTower R A M']
   242	    [AddCommMonoid N'] [Module R N'] [Module A N'] [IsScalarTower R A N']
   243	    (f : M →ₗ[R] M') (g : N →ₗ[R] N') (m : M) (n : N) :

   263	/-! ## Quasi-coherence from basic-open section localization
   264	
   265	The affine tensor-section formula (see the module docstring) would give, for
   266	`A B : X.Modules` quasi-coherent and `V` affine, the fact that the section restriction
   267	`Γ(A ⊗ B, V) → Γ(A ⊗ B, D(f))` is `IsLocalizedModule (powers f)` (the affine tensor-section

   270	The lemma below
   271	packages the *converse* direction of `Scheme.Modules.isLocalizedModule_basicOpen`
   272	(`QuotScheme.lean`): a sheaf of modules whose section restrictions are localizations on all

   275	`pushforward_isQuasicoherent_over_affine`, and is exactly the criterion the 01CB
   276	(`tensorObj`/`sheafTensorObj`) instance feeds once the affine section-localization is in hand. -/
   277	
   278	open TopologicalSpace in
   279	/-- The family of all affine opens covers a scheme (for the opens Grothendieck topology).
   280	Reconstruction of the `private` `QuotScheme.coversTop_affineOpens`. -/

   283	      (fun U : S.affineOpens => U.1) := by
   284	  intro W y hy

   286	    TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp (Scheme.isBasis_affineOpens S) hy

   291	set_option maxHeartbeats 1600000 in
   292	-- The tilde-presentation transport + affine-cover `of_coversTop` assembly (mirroring
   293	-- `QuotScheme.pushforward_isQuasicoherent_over_affine`) needs heartbeat/instance headroom.
   294	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   295	/-- **Quasi-coherence from basic-open section localization** (the converse of
   296	`Scheme.Modules.isLocalizedModule_basicOpen`).  If for every affine open `U` and every
   297	`f : Γ(X, U)` the section restriction `restrictBasicOpenₗ M f : Γ(M, U) → Γ(M, X.basicOpen f)`
   298	exhibits the target as the localization of the source at `powers f`, then `M` is quasi-coherent.
   299	
   300	Quasi-coherence is local (`SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent.of_coversTop`) on the affine-opens
   301	cover; on each affine `U` the hypothesis feeds
   302	`isIso_fromTildeΓ_pullback_fromSpec_of_isLocalizedModule` to produce the P1 datum
   303	`IsIso (fromTildeΓ ((pullback hU.fromSpec).obj M))`, whose tilde presentation transports along

   305	This is the pushforward-free form of `Scheme.Modules.pushforward_isQuasicoherent`. -/
   306	theorem isQuasicoherent_of_isLocalizedModule_basicOpen (M : X.Modules)
   307	    (H : ∀ (U : X.Opens), IsAffineOpen U → ∀ (f : Γ(X, U)),
   308	      letI : Module Γ(X, U) Γ(M, X.basicOpen f) :=
   309	        Module.compHom _ (algebraMap Γ(X, U) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f))
   310	      letI : IsScalarTower Γ(X, U) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) Γ(M, X.basicOpen f) :=
   311	        IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_smul (fun _ _ => rfl)
   312	      IsLocalizedModule (Submonoid.powers f) (Scheme.Modules.restrictBasicOpenₗ M f)) :
   313	    M.IsQuasicoherent := by
   314	  haveI hslice : ∀ U : X.affineOpens, (M.over U.1).IsQuasicoherent := by
   315	    intro U
   316	    haveI hP1 : IsIso (Scheme.Modules.fromTildeΓ
   317	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.2.fromSpec).obj M)) :=
   318	      Scheme.Modules.isIso_fromTildeΓ_pullback_fromSpec_of_isLocalizedModule M U.2
   319	        (fun f' => H U.1 U.2 f')
   320	    -- global presentation of the `fromSpec`-pullback, via the tilde presentation
   321	    let eT' : tilde ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj
   322	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.2.fromSpec).obj M)).presheaf.obj (Opposite.op ⊤))
   323	        ≅ (Scheme.Modules.pullback U.2.fromSpec).obj M :=
   324	      @asIso _ _ _ _
   325	        (Scheme.Modules.fromTildeΓ ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.2.fromSpec).obj M)) hP1

   327	      SheafOfModules.Presentation.ofIsIso.{u} eT'.hom
   328	        (AlgebraicGeometry.presentationTilde.{u} _ Set.univ (by simp) _ (Submodule.span_eq _))

   330	    have hcomp : U.2.isoSpec.hom ≫ U.2.fromSpec = U.1.ι := by
   331	      rw [← U.2.isoSpec_inv_ι, Iso.hom_inv_id_assoc]

   333	      SheafOfModules.Presentation.ofIsIso.{u, u, u}
   334	        ((Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp U.2.isoSpec.hom U.2.fromSpec).app M ≪≫
   335	          (Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr hcomp).app M).hom
   336	        (Scheme.Modules.presentationPullbackOfSchemeIso U.2.isoSpec.symm
   337	          ((Scheme.Modules.pullback U.2.fromSpec).obj M) P_M')

    12	/-!
    13	# Tensor products in `Scheme.Modules`
    14	
    15	The relative Picard group law sends two line bundles to their tensor product.
    16	At the pinned Mathlib revision, tensor products are available for presheaves of
    17	modules but not directly for `Scheme.Modules`. This file supplies the required
    18	scheme-level operations:
    19	
    20	1. a binary tensor-product operation
    21	   `⊗ : Scheme.Modules X × Scheme.Modules X → Scheme.Modules X`;
    22	2. the structure sheaf `O_X` as a designated unit object for `⊗`;
    23	3. an inverse operation on the full subcategory of invertible objects, i.e.
    24	   the dual `L⁻¹ = Hom(L, O_X)` of an invertible sheaf.
    25	
    26	The construction sheafifies `PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` on the small
    27	Zariski site. It develops functoriality, unitors, symmetry, associativity, duals,
    28	evaluation, local triviality, and compatibility with pullback and restriction.
    29	The tensor-inverse theorem is proved downstream in `TensorObjInverse.lean`.
    30	
    31	The principal blueprint-pinned declarations are:
    32	
    33	1. `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tensorObj` (def) — the substrate binary
    34	   operation `⊗ : Scheme.Modules X × Scheme.Modules X → Scheme.Modules X`,
    35	   lifting `PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` on underlying presheaves
    36	   composed with sheafification on the small Zariski site.
    37	   Per blueprint `def:scheme_modules_tensorobj`.
    38	
    39	2. `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tensorObj_functoriality` (def) — the
    40	   functorial action of `⊗` on morphisms: a pair `f : M ⟶ M'`, `g : N ⟶ N'`
    41	   determines `f ⊗ g : tensorObj M N ⟶ tensorObj M' N'`.
    42	   Per blueprint `lem:scheme_modules_tensorobj_functoriality`.
    43	
    44	A full `MonoidalCategory (Scheme.Modules X)` instance is deliberately omitted;
    45	the group law on isomorphism classes only needs the relevant coherence
    46	isomorphisms. See blueprint `rem:scheme_modules_monoidal_off_path`.
    47	
    48	## References
    49	
    50	Blueprint: `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_TensorObjSubstrate.tex`. Source:
    51	[Kleiman], "The Picard scheme", §2 (FGA Explained, Chapter 9, §9.2), and
    52	Stacks tags 01CR and 03DM. The underlying Mathlib construction is in
    53	`Mathlib.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.PresheafOfModules`
    54	(`PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj`).
    55	
    56	## Sub-module layout
    57	
    58	Supporting constructions live under `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/TensorObjSubstrate/`:
    59	
    60	- `StalkTensor.lean` proves the stalk tensor comparison.
    61	- `Vestigial.lean` contains auxiliary local-injectivity and stalk constructions.
    62	- `PresheafInternalHom.lean` develops the presheaf algebra used here:
    63	  `RestrictScalarsRingIsoTensor`, lax-monoidal `restrictScalars`, pushforward
    64	  adjunction (H1), `StrongMonoidalRestrictScalars` (H2), `InternalHom`, `Dual`.
    65	-/
    66	
    67	set_option autoImplicit false
    68	
    69	universe u
    70	
    71	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory
    72

    74	
    75	namespace Scheme

    78	
    79	/-! ## §1. The substrate tensor-product operation -/
    80	
    81	/-- **The substrate operation `⊗` on `Scheme.Modules X`.**
    82	
    83	For a scheme `X` and `M, N : X.Modules`, the tensor product
    84	`M ⊗_X N : X.Modules` is the sheafification of the presheaf-of-modules tensor
    85	product `PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` of the underlying presheaves of
    86	`M` and `N` (affine-locally `(M ⊗_X N)(Spec A) = M(Spec A) ⊗_A N(Spec A)`).
    87	
    88	Per blueprint `def:scheme_modules_tensorobj`. The body lifts
    89	`PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` through the sheafification functor on
    90	the small Zariski site of `X`. -/
    91	noncomputable def tensorObj {X : Scheme.{u}} (M N : X.Modules) : X.Modules :=
    92	  ((PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).obj
    93	      (PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj (R := X.presheaf) M.val N.val) :
    94	    SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf)
    95	
    96	/-- **Functoriality of `⊗_X`.**
    97	
    98	A pair of morphisms `f : M ⟶ M'` and `g : N ⟶ N'` in `X.Modules` determines a
    99	morphism `f ⊗ g : tensorObj M N ⟶ tensorObj M' N'`, compatible with identities
   100	and composition; the assignment `(M, N) ↦ tensorObj M N` thereby extends to a
   101	bifunctor `X.Modules × X.Modules ⥤ X.Modules` natural in both arguments.
   102	
   103	Per blueprint `lem:scheme_modules_tensorobj_functoriality`. The body inherits
   104	the morphism action from `PresheafOfModules.Monoidal.tensorObj` under
   105	sheafification. -/
   106	noncomputable def tensorObj_functoriality {X : Scheme.{u}} {M M' N N' : X.Modules}
   107	    (f : M ⟶ M') (g : N ⟶ N') : tensorObj M N ⟶ tensorObj M' N' :=
   108	  (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).map
   109	    (MonoidalCategory.tensorHom
   110	      (C := _root_.PresheafOfModules (X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)) f.val g.val)
   111	
   112	/-- **`⊗`-invertibility of an `𝒪_X`-module.** (Blueprint
   113	`def:scheme_modules_isinvertible`.) `M : X.Modules` is `⊗`-invertible when it
   114	admits a tensor inverse: an object `N` with `M ⊗_X N ≅ 𝒪_X`, where
   115	`𝒪_X = SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf` is the designated unit. This is the
   116	scheme-level analogue of Mathlib's `Module.Invertible`; the predicate carries its
   117	inverse witness existentially, so the dual needed by the relative Picard group
   118	law is definitional. -/
   119	def IsInvertible {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules) : Prop :=
   120	  ∃ N : X.Modules, Nonempty (tensorObj M N ≅ SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)
   121	
   122	/-- **The sheaf-level dual `M^∨ := ℋom_{𝒪_X}(M, 𝒪_X)`** of an `𝒪_X`-module.
   123	
   124	For a scheme `X` and `M : X.Modules`, the dual `dual M : X.Modules` is the
   125	sheafification of the presheaf-of-modules dual `PresheafOfModules.dual` of the
   126	underlying presheaf of `M` (the internal hom into the structure presheaf,
   127	`M^∨(U) = ℋom_{𝒪_X|_U}(M|_U, 𝒪_X|_U)`).
   128	
   129	The construction is the dual analogue of `tensorObj`: apply
   130	`PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 …)` on the small Zariski site to the presheaf dual
   131	`PresheafOfModules.dual M.val`. The scheme's structure presheaf `X.presheaf` is
   132	`CommRingCat`-valued over the single-universe topological site `Opens X`, hence is
   133	exactly the base `R₀ : Dᵒᵖ ⥤ CommRingCat.{u}` that `PresheafOfModules.dual`
   134	requires (the value `M^∨(U) = M|_U ⟶ R|_U` is an `R(U)`-module, needing
   135	commutativity) — no CommRingCat/RingCat re-bridging is needed, since
   136	`tensorObj` already takes `(R := X.presheaf)` over the same CommRingCat presheaf
   137	and `X.ringCatSheaf.obj = X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat` definitionally.
   138	
   139	The sheafification functor already lands in `SheafOfModules`, so no manual
   140	`Presheaf.IsSheaf` / sheaf-condition descent is needed (sheafifying an already-sheaf
   141	gives an iso object; this is the file's convention, matching `tensorObj`).
   142	
   143	Per blueprint `lem:internal_hom_isSheaf` (§`sec:tensorobj_dual_infra`); Stacks
   144	tags 01CM (internal hom into a sheaf is a sheaf) / 01CR item 2. This is the
   145	`⊗`-inverse candidate of an invertible sheaf, feeding `exists_tensorObj_inverse`. -/
   146	noncomputable def dual {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules) : X.Modules :=
   147	  ((PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).obj
   148	      (PresheafOfModules.dual (R₀ := X.presheaf) M.val) :
   149	    SheafOfModules X.ringCatSheaf)
   150	
   151	/-- **The sheaf-level dual is contravariantly functorial in isomorphisms.** An isomorphism
   152	`e : M ≅ M'` in `X.Modules` induces `dual M' ≅ dual M`, obtained by sheafifying the presheaf-level
   153	dual iso `PresheafOfModules.dualIsoOfIso` of the underlying presheaf isomorphism. This is the
   154	reusable "dual respects isos" ingredient (the dual analogue of `tensorObjIsoOfIso`) feeding the
   155	assembly of `dual_isLocallyTrivial`: a trivialisation `L.restrict f ≅ 𝒪` yields, contravariantly,
   156	`dual 𝒪 ≅ dual (L.restrict f)`. -/
   157	noncomputable def dualIsoOfIso {X : Scheme.{u}} {M M' : X.Modules} (e : M ≅ M') :
   158	    dual M' ≅ dual M :=
   159	  (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).mapIso
   160	    (PresheafOfModules.dualIsoOfIso (R₀ := X.presheaf)
   161	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).mapIso e))
   162	
   163	/-! ## §2. Why no full monoidal-category instance is needed
   164	
   165	The full `MonoidalCategory (X.Modules)` instance is deliberately not built. Per
   166	blueprint `rem:scheme_modules_monoidal_off_path`,
   167	the relative Picard group law is a structure on *isomorphism classes* of line
   168	bundles — every group axiom is a `Nonempty (… ≅ …)` proposition, so no monoidal
   169	coherence and no `MonoidalClosed` structure is consumed. The group law is built
   170	directly on the line-bundle subcategory from the coherence isomorphisms below,
   171	mirroring Mathlib's `CommRing.Pic`. -/
   172	
   173	/-! ## §3. The lift through `LineBundle.OnProduct`
   174	
   175	The following helper lemmas record the lift of the substrate to the
   176	locally-trivial subcategory used by the relative Picard consumer. -/
   177	
   178	/-- **The substrate operation respects isomorphisms in both arguments.**
   179	
   180	A pair of isomorphisms `e : M ≅ M'` and `e' : N ≅ N'` in `X.Modules` induces an
   181	isomorphism `tensorObj M N ≅ tensorObj M' N'`, obtained by sheafifying the
   182	tensor product (in the presheaf-of-modules monoidal category) of the underlying
   183	presheaf isomorphisms `e.val`, `e'.val`. Its `hom` is
   184	`tensorObj_functoriality e.hom e'.hom`. This is the reusable functor-of-isos
   185	ingredient feeding `tensorObj_isLocallyTrivial`. -/
   186	noncomputable def tensorObjIsoOfIso {X : Scheme.{u}} {M M' N N' : X.Modules}
   187	    (e : M ≅ M') (e' : N ≅ N') : tensorObj M N ≅ tensorObj M' N' :=
   188	  (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).mapIso
   189	    (MonoidalCategory.tensorIso
   190	      (C := _root_.PresheafOfModules (X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat))
   191	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).mapIso e)
   192	      ((SheafOfModules.forget X.ringCatSheaf).mapIso e'))
   193	
   194	/-- **The substrate tensor of the structure sheaf with itself is the structure
   195	sheaf.**
   196	
   197	`tensorObj 𝒪_X 𝒪_X ≅ 𝒪_X`, where `𝒪_X = SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf` is the
   198	designated unit object. Built from the presheaf-level left unitor
   199	`λ_ (𝟙_)` (the unit of the `PresheafOfModules` monoidal category is exactly
   200	`SheafOfModules.unit.val`) under sheafification, composed with the
   201	sheafification-adjunction counit isomorphism on the (already-sheaf) unit. -/
   202	noncomputable def tensorObj_unit_iso {X : Scheme.{u}} :
   203	    tensorObj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)
   204	      ≅ SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf := by
   205	  -- Use the explicit monoidal structure so the second tensor factor remains the literal
   206	  -- structure-presheaf carrier; this avoids an unnecessary definitional equality between
   207	  -- two presentations of the monoidal unit.
   208	  exact
   209	    (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).mapIso
   210	        ((PresheafOfModules.monoidalCategoryStruct (R := X.presheaf)).leftUnitor
   211	          (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf).val) ≪≫
   212	      (asIso (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).counit).app
   213	        (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf)
   214	
   215	/-- **Left unitor for `⊗_X`.** `𝒪_X ⊗_X M ≅ M`. (Blueprint
   216	`lem:tensorobj_unit_iso`, left half, `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tensorObj_left_unitor`.)
   217	Sheafification of the presheaf-level left unitor `λ_ M.val`, composed with the
   218	sheafification counit identifying `sheafification M.val` with the (already-sheaf)
   219	`M`. The cheap `mapIso` pattern; uses no abstract pullback. -/
   220	noncomputable def tensorObj_left_unitor {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules) :
   221	    tensorObj (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) M ≅ M :=
   222	  (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).mapIso
   223	      ((PresheafOfModules.monoidalCategoryStruct (R := X.presheaf)).leftUnitor M.val) ≪≫
   224	    (asIso (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).counit).app M
   225	
   226	/-- **Right unitor for `⊗_X`.** `M ⊗_X 𝒪_X ≅ M`. (Blueprint
   227	`lem:tensorobj_unit_iso`, right half, `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tensorObj_right_unitor`.)
   228	Sheafification of the presheaf-level right unitor `ρ_ M.val`, composed with the
   229	sheafification counit. -/
   230	noncomputable def tensorObj_right_unitor {X : Scheme.{u}} (M : X.Modules) :
   231	    tensorObj M (SheafOfModules.unit X.ringCatSheaf) ≅ M :=
   232	  (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).mapIso
   233	      ((PresheafOfModules.monoidalCategoryStruct (R := X.presheaf)).rightUnitor M.val) ≪≫
   234	    (asIso (PresheafOfModules.sheafificationAdjunction (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).counit).app M
   235	
   236	/-- **Braiding for `⊗_X`.** `M ⊗_X N ≅ N ⊗_X M`. (Blueprint
   237	`lem:tensorobj_comm_iso`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tensorObj_braiding`.)
   238	The presheaf-of-modules monoidal category is symmetric; its braiding `β_ M.val
   239	N.val` sheafifies to the asserted isomorphism by the cheap `mapIso` pattern. -/
   240	noncomputable def tensorObj_braiding {X : Scheme.{u}} (M N : X.Modules) :
   241	    tensorObj M N ≅ tensorObj N M :=
   242	  (PresheafOfModules.sheafification (R := X.ringCatSheaf) (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)).mapIso
   243	    (BraidedCategory.braiding
   244	      (C := _root_.PresheafOfModules (X.presheaf ⋙ forget₂ CommRingCat RingCat)) M.val N.val)
   245	
   246	/-- **Associator for `⊗_X`.** (Blueprint
   247	`lem:tensorobj_assoc_iso`, `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.tensorObj_assoc_iso`.)
   248	For arbitrary `M, N, P : X.Modules` there is an isomorphism
   249	`(M ⊗_X N) ⊗_X P ≅ M ⊗_X (N ⊗_X P)`. This is the objectwise existence-of-iso datum the
   250	group law consumes (associativity as a `Nonempty (… ≅ …)`).
   251	
   252	No flatness or local-triviality hypothesis is used. Instead, the proof uses stability of
   253	the class inverted by sheafification under left and right whiskering.
   254	Writing `a = PresheafOfModules.sheafification (𝟙 X.ringCatSheaf.obj)` and `η` the
   255	sheafification-adjunction unit, the three-step composite is:
   256	  1. `a(η_{M.val ⊗ᵖ N.val} ▷ P.val)` is iso, giving
   257	     `(M ⊗ N) ⊗ P ≅ a((M.val⊗N.val) ⊗ P.val)`;
   258	  2. `a.mapIso α : a((M.val⊗N.val)⊗P.val) ≅ a(M.val⊗(N.val⊗P.val))`, `α` the
   259	     presheaf-of-modules associator;
   260	  3. `a(M.val ◁ η_{N.val ⊗ᵖ P.val})` is iso, giving
   261	     `a(M.val⊗(N.val⊗P.val)) ≅ M ⊗ (N ⊗ P)`.
   262	Steps 1/3 invert the whiskered sheafification unit via the flatness-free
   263	`PresheafOfModules.W_whisker{Right,Left}_of_W` (η = `toSheafify ∈ J.W`, and `J.W` is

   612	    {X S X' S' : Scheme.{u}} {f : X ⟶ S} {g : S' ⟶ S} {g' : X' ⟶ X} {f' : X' ⟶ S'}

   617	    Mono ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g').map (Limits.kernel.ι q)) := by
